 APPEAL UNDER SECTION 19 OF THE INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY ORGANIZATION OF PAKISTAN ACT, 2012 READ WITH ALL OTHER ENABLING PROVISIONS OF THE LAW AGAINST THE ORDER AND DECREE DATED 26.02.2025 PASSED IN SUIT NO. 116/IPT/2019 BY THE INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY TRIBUNAL, LAHORE 
 
 
 Respectfully sheweth : 
 
 That the addresses of the parties have sufficiently been provided in the title of the present Appeal for properly affecting the process of service of notice(s). 
 
 That the Appellant is a private limited company incorporated under the laws of Pakistan. The present Appeal is being filed by the Appellant through its duly authorized representative namely Mr. Salman Rashid Sheikh , who is well conversant with the facts of the case, and has been duly authorized in this regard. 
 
 [Certified true copy of the Board Resolution is attached herewith as Annexure “ A ” ] 
 
 That the Appellant is engaged in the business of providing real estate marketing services, which include s , inter alia , digital solutions, real estate portal and services to real estate developers, including inter alia IT and IT-enabled services and other related services such as branding, ATL and BTL activities (the “ Business ”). The Appellant is carrying on the Business under the tradename of “Zameen.com” and “ Zameen Media” (the “ Tradename ”). The Appellant is well known in Pakistan for its quality of ser vice, innovation and efficiency. It is pertinent to mention here that on account of the effort of the Appellant from its inception till date, the Appellant’s brand of services, along with the Appellant’s tradename and trademarks, have acquired a colossal amount of goodwill recognition, both within and outside Pakistan. 
 
 That an integral part of the Appellant’s Business consists of operating and maintaining an electronic/online real estate portal under the dom ain name ‘www.zameen.com ” (the “ Website ”), through which the Appellant offers and provides numerous services that are part of its Business. In this regard, it is pertinent to note that the Appellant’s Website was one of the first of its kind in Pakistan. The same has had a significant impact on the real estate market in Pakistan which earlier was a highly conservative market, and primarily operated through offline means. Due to the hard work, persistence, and perseverance of the management of the Appellant , the Website has hosted over 51 million property listings, 110 million monthly page-views, and more than 5.9 million subscribed members. Thus, it would not be out of place to point out that the Appellant is not only the market leader, but can also be credited with introducing this kind of IT and IT-enabled services at such a grand scale in the country. 
 
 That in this regard , it is pointed out that over the years, the Appellant has used and registered various trademarks and names for its business (the “ Trademarks ”). These are vital components in the design, color scheme, and outlay of the Website. The same has resulted in great customer reliance and satisfaction, and has led to the Appellant’s Trademarks being trusted and well-known marks in the real estate market in Pakistan and abroad. The services being provided by the Appellant are rendered using the Trademarks, and any promotional material/advertisements/official document/correspondence of or by the Appellant carry the Trademarks of the Appellant, along wi th other distinctive features. I n order to safeguard its proprietary rights vis-à-vis the Trademarks, and to curtail any unauthorized use thereof, the Appellant has time and again sought registration of the Trademarks in its use under different classes through applications filed with , inter alia , the Trade Marks Registry of the Intellectual Property Organization of Pakistan . The details of the Appellant’s Trademarks are as follow:

 [Copies of the certificate of registration of the Trademark are attached herewith as Annexure “ B ” ] 
 
 
 That the Respondents No. 1 is a private limited company incorporated under the laws of Pakistan and the Respondent No. 2 is the co-founder/direct or sales of the Respondent No. 1. The Respondent s No. 1 &amp; 2 have been carrying on their business of providing real estate services, including, but not limited to, through website, internet and social media by using a deceptively similar tradename of “ Zameen Homes” in addition to their logo. In this regard it is noted that the Respondent s No. 1 &amp; 2 adopted marks such as “ Zameen Homes” and “zameenhomes.com”, and were using the slogan “Hum Janein Har Jagha ”, which are phonetically phonemically similar to the Appellant’s Trademarks. The mark of the Respondent s No. 1 &amp; 2 consisting of the letters “Z” and “H” boxed in a shape representing a house is confusing and deceptively similar to the Appellant’s Tradenames and Trademark since it has the same distinctive styling, design, and layout, along with using the same primary letter “Z” and th e same imagery as the Appellant’s mark consisting of the letter “Z” boxed in a shape representing a house. This is in clear infringement of the Appellant’s Trademark No.334698 consisting of the words “Zameen.com Pakistan’s No.1 Property Website” partially boxed in a shape representing a house in Class 42, which are duly registered with the Trade Marks Registry. 
 
 
 That on account of the infringement by the Respondent s No. 1 &amp; 2 , the Appellant filed a Suit No. 116/IPT/2019 titled “ Zameen Media (Private) Limited vs. Zameen Homes (Private) Limited, etc.” (the “ Suit ”) before the Intellectual Property Tribunal, Lahore, for declaration and permanent injunction against the infringement, unauthorized adoption and use of, inter alia , the Trademarks of the Appellant by the Respondents No. 1 &amp; 2 . It may be noted that the actions of the Respondent s No. 1 &amp; 2 amount ed to a sheer violation of the Appellant ’ s exclusive proprietary rights, including, but not limited to, infringement of the Appellant ’ s Trademark (s) which have been duly registered with the Trade Marks Registry, particularly the Appellant’s Trademark s registered under Trademark No. 504442, 504443, 504454, 504455 and 504456. 
 
 
 That the Suit was filed before the Intellectual Property Tribunal, Lahore on 08.07.2019 whereby the Respondent No. 3 after hearing the Appellant ordered for issuance of notices/ summons in the name of the Respondent s No. 1 &amp; 2 . Thereafter, the matter was fixed for hearing on 22.07.2019; however, no one appeared on behalf of the Respondent s No. 1 &amp; 2 . 
 
 
 That along with the Suit, the Appellant had filed an Application for temporary injunction under Order 39 Rule 1 &amp; 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908. In this regard, the Tribunal vide O rder dated 24.07.2019, granted temporary injunction and restrained the Respondents No. 1 &amp; 2 from using or advertising the marks of trade name and the Zameen Homes logo, which were identical and deceptively similar to the Appellant ’ s Trademarks. 
 
 
 That thereafter , the matter was fixed for hearing on 06.08.2019, 13.09.2019 and 09.10.2019; however, the Respondents No. 1 &amp; 2 failed to appear before the learned Court. During this time, several other summons were also served and the matter was advertised in the newspaper for the procurement of Respondents No. 1 &amp; 2 . On account of the non-appearance of the Respondents No. 1 &amp; 2 , the Tribunal vide Order dated 30.10.2019 ordered for ex-parte proceedings against the Respondents No. 1 &amp; 2 . Thereafter, the matter was fixed for ex-parte evidence. 
 
 
 That it may be noted that the witnesses of the Appellant appeared before the Tribunal at multiple times; however, on account of the absence of the Respondent No. 3 on the said dates, the evidence of the Appellant could not be recorded and the reader failed to record the attendance of the witness ( es ) . 
 
 
 That on 08.01.2025, the matter was adjourned in routine for evidence and the next date of hearing was fixed for 26.02.2025 . In this regard, it is pointed out that the witnesses of the Appellant namely ( i ) Mr. Salman Rashid Sheikh and (ii) Mr. Ali Singay could not be available before the Tribunal as Mr. Ali Singay had left the Appellant company and was not in Pakistan while the other witness Mr. Salman Rashid Sheikh was not in Lahore. On this account, the Appellant requested that the matter be adjourned to another date so that the evidence of the Appellant be recorde d. However, the Respondent No. 3 failed to adjourn the matter and passed the Order and Decree dated 26.02.2025 (“ Impugned Order and Decree ”) whereby the Appellant’s right for producing ex-parte evidence was illegally and unlawfully closed and the Suit was dismissed for want of evidence. 
 
 [ Copy of the ( i ) record of the Suit; (ii) Order Sheet; and (iii) Original Impugned Order and Decree dated 26.02.2025 are attached herewith as Annexures “C -1 ” , “C -2 ” , and “C -3 ” respectively ] 
 
 
 That the Appellant stands aggrieved of the Impugned Order and Decree passed by the Respondent No. 3 as the same is illegal, unlawful and has been passed in ignorance of the settled dicta of the Superior Courts of Pakistan . In view thereof, the Impugned Order is liable to be set aside on the following grounds: 
 
 GROUNDS: 
 
 
 That the Respondent No. 3 has erred in law by passing the Impugned Order and Decree without iss uing any warning and intimating to the Appellant that failure to produce ex- parte evidence would result in closure of Appellant’s right to produce evidence and the dismissal of the Suit. It is settled law that before initiating a penal action, a warning has to be given to the concerned party. Since, this pre-requisite has not been complied by the Respondent No. 3 , in view thereof, the Impugned Order and Decree are liable to be set aside. 
 
 
 That it is a settled principle of law that the court is required to afford the party a clear and unequivocal opportunity to cure the default and must duly intimate the consequence of non-compliance of the same . In the absence of such a final warning, the action taken is of no legal effect. Hence, the dismissal of the Suit amounts to a violation of the principles of natural justice and due process. From a reading of the previous Order dated 08.01.2025 (which was the previous order before passing the Impugned Order), it is clear that no such war n ing was given by the Respondent No. 3 in informing the Appellant of the consequence of failure to produce ex - parte evidence would result in dismissal of the Suit . Therefore, the Impugned Order and Decree are liable to be set aside. 
 
 
 That the Impugned Order and Decree have been passed without considering that the Appellant had made out a prima facie case substantiated with all relevant evidence and details pertaining to the Suit. That it is settled principle of law that if a party has a prima facie case on merits then it would be within safe administration of justice to exercise discretion towards dispensation of justice. The Appellant has suffered irreparable damage to its goodwill and reputation and has incurred a loss of upto Rs . 50,000,000 /- . This damage cannot be overlook ed on procedural irregularities. However, the Respondent No. 3 has failed to consider these material aspects and has passed the Impugned Order and Decree illegally. In view thereof, the Impugned Order and Decree are liable to be set aside. 
 
 
 That the failure to complete evidence was neither deliberate nor intentional. The Suit has been dismissed vide the Impugned Order and Decree without issuing a final warning to the Appellant that failure to produce ex-parte evidence on the next date would result in closure of its right and dismissal of the Suit. It is settled law that penal action could not be taken without providing a final opportunity to the party. Hence, it is clear that the Impugned Order and Decree are against the settled dicta of the Superior Courts and against the principles of natural justice. Keeping in view the above, the Impugned Order and Decree are liable to be set aside. 
 
 
 That it is settled law that a matter should be decided on merits rather than technicalities. The Impugned Order and Decree have been passed without considering the record of the Suit. In view thereof, the Impugned Order and Decree are liable to be set aside. 
 
 
 That it is specifically averred that the Impugned Order and Decree have been issued without any application of independent mind and in ignorance of the settled dicta of the Superior Court s and the law. Without prejudice to any other ground taken herein, it may be noted that it is well settled law that an authority exercising discretionary powers is required to exercise the same reasonably, justly, fairly, and on the basis of relevant considerations having legal nexus with the object of the law. Such principles are to be read into statutes as guiding principles to regulate the exercise of powers conferred on functionaries of the State and are so fundamental in character that they need not be provided in a statute itself. In this regard, it is most respectfully submitted that Respondent No. 3 purported exercise of power of passing the Impugned Order is in violation of Articles 4, 8, and 10A of the Constitution as well as Section 24A of the General Clauses Act, 1894. In light of this, the Impugned Order and Decree are liable to be set aside and declared as illegal and unlawful . 
 
 That the Petitioner seeks permission to raise further grounds at the time of hearing 
 
 PRAYER: 
 
 In view of the above, it is most respectfully prayed that the instant Appeal may kindly be accepted and the Impugned Order and Decree dated 2 6 . 0 2.202 5 may kindly be set aside.
